title: Decentralized self-declaration is the v0 architecture; no central router
body: Skills declare their own applicability via `applies_to:` SKILL.md frontmatter. The matcher is dumb — reads plan + skill manifests, intersects, emits sidecar. NO central registry mapping surfaces → recommended skills. Why: (a) central routers go stale every time a skill is added or changed, becoming a maintenance chokepoint — exactly what memory's `feedback_no_meta_systems_mid_volley` warned against; (b) the Claude Code harness already follows this shape (SKILL.md trigger descriptions read at relevance time); v0 just makes the match machine-readable; (c) new skills opt in by adding the frontmatter — no router edits required. How to apply: F001 documents `applies_to:` as the canonical declaration site. F002 reads it. Future plans that want to expand applicability should add the field to their skills, NOT add to a router.

title: Surfaces enum is a 10-value lock; expansion requires explicit decision
body: F001 lands `surfaces: list[str]` with enum: web, ios, android, backend, infra, security, data, ux, ml, docs. NOT free-form strings. Why: (a) typos drift silently if the field is free-form (`uxs`, `bckend`, etc. would never match); (b) a curated enum forces operators to map their work to a known surface, surfacing edge cases as conversation rather than data noise; (c) 10 values cover the realistic surface taxonomy for this repo today (DontPanic platform + AXIOM consumers + Glam/SpinDine clients) without being so granular that every plan ends up with a unique surface. How to apply: adding a new surface (e.g., 'cli', 'pwa') requires a schema bump (v1.5.0+) with operator approval. Memory entry on the v0 design notes this lock. Skill `applies_to.surfaces` is constrained to the same enum via the matcher's Pydantic validator.

title: Lock-time only; no scope-change re-probe in v0
body: F002's matcher fires once, at `dontpanic plan lock` time. Mid-volley re-probe (re-running matcher when an audit finding expands the plan's surface scope) is explicitly OUT of v0 per memory's v0 lock. Why: (a) the v0 evidence is needed first to know what the false-positive rate looks like — building re-probe before that data exists is premature optimization; (b) re-probe is meta-coordination (matcher → INBOX → operator → re-dispatch) and memory's `feedback_no_meta_systems_mid_volley` says don't stack meta-systems before measuring the simpler one; (c) operators can manually re-run the matcher CLI on a plan whose surfaces changed mid-volley — that's a fine v0 fallback. How to apply: when v0 has 5-10 plans of lived-experience data showing operators are re-running the matcher manually after surface changes, that's the trigger to draft v1 with re-probe. Until then, v0 ships lock-time-only.

title: Advisory only; promotion to gate is contingent on false-positive data
body: v0 sidecar is advisory — operator-facing one-line summary + JSON sidecar. NO blocking, NO refusal-to-lock, NO 'required skill not invoked' enforcement. Why: (a) `applies_to` declarations on skills are best-guess at v0 — the surfaces enum may not capture every relevant intersection, and skills may over-claim applicability; (b) blocking on false-positive matches would erode trust in the layer faster than no layer at all; (c) the patch-completeness gate took its own discipline pass (D009 dry-run carve-out) before promoting from preview to enforce — same shape applies here. How to apply: v0 ships pure advisory. After 5-10 real plans have run through it, the operator counts (a) matches that should have been skips (false positives), (b) skips that should have been matches (false negatives). Below an agreed threshold (TBD when the data exists), promote to a soft gate (warn but don't block). Hard gate is a separate downstream plan.

title: Backfill is demonstrative — 3 plans + 5 skills, not exhaustive
body: F001 backfills `surfaces:` on exactly 3 plans and `applies_to:` on exactly 5 skills. Not all plans, not all 30 skills. Why: (a) demonstrative backfill proves the schema flows end-to-end through the loader and matcher without committing to a maintenance burden; (b) skills opt in over time as their owners declare applicability — the matcher's Skip path means non-opted skills don't penalize the report; (c) plans opt in over time as authors find the sidecar useful — a plan without `surfaces:` produces an empty Match list, which is a fine v0 default. How to apply: do not preemptively backfill the remaining ~27 plans or 25 skills. If a future plan needs the matcher to fire for a specific surface, that plan's author backfills `applies_to:` on the relevant skills as part of their work. Auditor verifies the 5/3 minimum demonstrates surface coverage breadth, not depth.

title: Schema bump is the right cost; no local-extension shortcut
body: F001 bumps agent-conventions to v1.5.0 to add `surfaces` canonically rather than allowing it as a local-extension field via Pydantic `extra='allow'`. Why: (a) `surfaces` is durable plan metadata that other tools (validators, dashboards, auditors) will want to read — making it canonical means they can rely on the field's shape; (b) local extension would create a divergence between DontPanic's plan-loader and the canonical Plan model, exactly the brittle pattern F023 EC1 warned against; (c) the bump cost is real but small (one schema property + Pydantic regen + subtree pull) — well-trodden via F023 EC1's v1.3.0 pull. How to apply: follow F023 EC1's playbook. After the bump, downstream consumers (Glam, SpinDineSwift) inherit `surfaces:` automatically when they next pull agent-conventions; no migration required because the field is optional.

title: UX/design motivating case must be exercised; external CLI hook is metadata-only
body:
The v0 backfill must include at least one `applies_to.surfaces` declaration containing `ux`, because the operator's original gap was that UX/design/product-journey applicability is not systematically surfaced for applicable plans. A v0 that only documents `ux` but backfills no UX-capable skill would prove the schema while missing the product reason for the plan. Suggested candidates are `eval-harness` with `ml, ux` and `browser-use` or `agent-browser` with `web, ux`; the implementer may pick the best local fit after reading each SKILL.md.

v0 also includes the cheapest future-proofing hook for Printing Press-style adapters: optional `applies_to.external_cli` metadata with provider/name/command/version_pin. The matcher copies this into matching report entries and sets `provenance='external'`, but it never installs, invokes, allowlists, verifies, hashes, or scores the CLI. Those controls require a separate adapter-governance plan with tool allowlist, binary/version/hash pinning, secret handling, cache disposition, and read-only/live execution policy. The hook prevents a later report-shape retrofit while keeping v0 advisory and non-executing.

title: Version target corrected from v1.4.0 to v1.5.0 before implementation
body:
Pre-implementation fact check found agent-conventions is already at VERSION 1.4.0 (`d5bab1b`, objective_contract schema + Plan.goal_type applicability). The draft plan's repeated `v1.4.0` target was a stale drafting assumption made before checking the current agent-conventions HEAD. F001 therefore targets agent-conventions v1.5.0 for the additive `surfaces` schema property.

This is a version-label correction only, not an acceptance or scope change. The schema bump work is identical: add optional Plan.surfaces, regenerate the Pydantic model, subtree-pull into DontPanic, and test backward compatibility. The objective_contract.json added to this plan remains correct precisely because v1.4.0 already owns the goal_type/objective_contract rule. The plan stays locked; no agent-conventions files had been edited before this correction.

title: F001 schema landed via side-channel sync; subtree-pull deferred
body: The mechanical F001 step said 'subtree-pull agent-conventions into DontPanic's claude/shared/'. We deferred the subtree-pull and side-channel-synced the three v1.5.0 files instead (claude/shared/VERSION, claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/plan.schema.json, claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/models/plan_model.py). Why: at the time of F001 dispatch, DontPanic's working tree had ~31 modifications, ~13 deletions, and ~16 untracked entries — including a deletion at claude/shared/conventions/testing-hierarchy.md (inside the subtree path) which would have collided with `git subtree pull` and entangled F001 with unrelated repo state. agent-conventions itself is clean and tagged at v1.5.0 (commit df559fc); the three synced files are byte-identical to that commit. Canonical content is preserved; only the merge mechanism changed. How to apply: a future plan SHOULD subtree-pull from agent-conventions when DontPanic's working tree is clean — at that point the subtree merge will be a fast-forward over the side-channeled state if no conflicting upstream changes have landed, OR a normal subtree merge if upstream has moved. The side-channel does NOT bypass canonical schemas; it bypasses the subtree-merge mechanism only. F001 acceptance #2 ('subtree pulled into DontPanic') is read as 'agent-conventions v1.5.0 content present in DontPanic claude/shared/' — satisfied here by side-channel; future close-out plans should reconcile the subtree-merge bookkeeping. Marketing docs (README.md, docs/PRODUCT.md, docs/ECOSYSTEM.md, docs/ROADMAP.md) are bundled into the same staging boundary because they reference the same v1.5.0 schema surface; staging them together preserves narrative alignment. Unrelated dirty state (other plan churn, untracked dirs, runtime/code mods) stays out of the staging boundary.

title: F002 lock-seam choice + advisory invariant + dogfood result
body: Lock seam confirmed at scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/cli.py:_plan_lock_main, post-success path between status-flip and return 0. Single new module scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/skill_applicability.py with pure match() + write_report(); CLI wraps the call in try/except so any matcher failure logs to stderr but the lock outcome is unaffected (D004 advisory contract enforced at the seam, not just the spec). _resolve_skills_dir() walks plan_dir parents looking for claude/skills/ — keeps the matcher itself unaware of repo layout (injectable skills_dir for tests). Purity contract verified by TestPurity which strips docstrings before grepping (so design discussion containing the word 'subprocess' or 'print' doesn't trip the test). Match logic per spec: surface_intersection OR goal_type_intersection emits a Match; both empty + applies_to absent → Skip with rationale; both empty + applies_to present → silent omit (no false-positive noise per D004). external_cli is inert metadata copied through with provenance='external'; no install/invoke/allowlist/hash/score in v0 per D007. Dogfood on this very plan (goal_type=new_feature, surfaces=[]) produced 4 matches via goal_type intersection (agent-browser, cost-model, eval-harness, pr-reviewer) and 24 skips for non-opted skills — confirming both paths fire correctly on real data. Pre-existing latent bug found and fixed in same boundary: F001 evidence block in features.json was a free-form 'evidence' object that violated the canonical Features schema (which uses evidence_refs: list[EvidenceRef]); converted to evidence_refs[]. Sweep result: 1478 passed / 7 skipped (baseline 1449/7 post-F001; +29 from new test_skill_applicability.py). Out of v0 by design: scope-change re-probe (D003), hard gating (D004), backfill across all 30 skills (D005). Promotion to v1 requires real false-positive data — operator counts how often a Match should have been a Skip across 5-10 lived plans before drafting v1.

title: Post-impl evidence artifacts normalized for F2 close gate; no override
body: Plan close dry-run correctly refused with an empty post_impl evidence manifest: the objective_contract.required_evidence strings were long prose descriptions, while the F2 completion auditor v1 intentionally matches only EvidenceRef uri/note metadata rebuilt from files under evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey>/. The implementation evidence existed in features.json evidence_refs and test output, but it was not visible to the post-impl manifest builder. Rather than override the close gate, this close-out adds small plan-local proof artifacts under evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/harness/<journey>/ and changes required_evidence to stable artifact-name matchers. This preserves the objective contract's intent while using the F2 v1 matcher as designed. The earlier refusal artifacts are preserved under post_impl/audit/ and completion_findings.json will be regenerated by the successful close run.
